item: Which text imposes publication of the petition: CPCA article 17 (third paragraph) on petitions concerning real property or a real right in it published under the law.
Does the duty apply only when the property or right is itself already published at the land registry (registered/titled property), or to every claim about real property?

Which claims fall under the duty: claims for rescission, annulment, cancellation or revocation of rights arising from published deeds (Decree 76-63 on the land register, article 85, from memory), or every claim concerning a published real right?

What exactly must be published: the petition opening the claim itself (a copy bearing the court's filing details), at the competent land registry office (المحافظة العقارية) of the property's location.
When must proof of publication be produced: at the first hearing at which the case is called.
What counts as proof: the published petition bearing the registrar's mention, or at least proof that it was deposited for publication (receipt of deposit).
Sanction: inadmissibility in form (عدم القبول شكلا) unless deposit for publication is proven.
Is the sanction raised by the court of its own motion, or only on the defendant's plea? Is it a matter of public order?
Can the defect be cured before the court rules (late production of the publication certificate)?
Does inadmissibility in form allow the claim to be filed again after publication?
Which claims about real property are outside the duty: claims about unpublished (non-titled, customary) property; personal claims for payment of rent or price; possession claims?

Are eviction claims of a tenant from a dwelling or professional premises subject to publication? (Probably not, since a lease right is not a published real right unless the lease is long and published.)
Are partition claims of co-owned published property subject to publication?
Are claims to annul or rescind a sale of a published property subject to publication (the classic case)?
Do pre-emption (الشفعة) claims require publication (civil code articles on pre-emption, from memory)?
Fees for publication at the land registry (registration and publication duties, finance laws) - not the court's business but needed in practice.
Effect of publication: the judgment, once published, is enforceable against third parties from the date of the petition's publication (priority / retroactivity of the publication of the judgment).
Duty to publish the judgment itself after it becomes final (Ordinance 75-74 and Decree 76-63, from memory).
Does the same duty apply on appeal or in the cassation stage (new petition on appeal)?
Does the duty apply before the administrative courts (CPCA article for administrative procedure referring to article 17)?
Interaction with the real property section of the court (القسم العقاري) and the territorial rule (court of the property's location) - shared modules court-sections and territorial-jurisdiction.
CPCA articles in the real-property chapter (around articles 511 to 529, from memory 519) - do they repeat or modify the publication rule?
Required documents: the petition copy with the land registry's publication stamp or deposit receipt; the title deed or a land-register extract (fiche) showing the property is published.
Who must publish: the plaintiff (or his lawyer) at his cost.
Is there any period for publication before the first hearing, or only the hearing as deadline?
Distinguish the duty to publish the petition (a procedural condition of admissibility) from the publication of deeds as a condition of the transfer of ownership (civil code article 793, from memory).
Distinguish the petition about a right resulting from a published deed from a claim to force the conclusion or publication of a sale (claim for the delivery of a deed).
Amendments: whether article 17 was amended after 2008 (Law 22-13 amending the CPCA, from memory) - check the current wording.
Does the dispute concern real property or a real right in real property (ownership, possession, co-ownership, partition, easement, mortgage)?
Is the property itself published at the land registry (محافظة عقارية), or is it unsurveyed/unpublished land held by customary or undated title?
Does the claim seek to cancel, rescind, annul, revoke or amend a right or a deed that was itself published at the land registry?
Does the claim concern a right published on the real-property register, so that the petition must be published?
Is the petition one of those listed for compulsory publication (annulment, rescission, revocation, resolution of a published deed)?
Who must carry out the publication: the plaintiff, his lawyer, or the court clerk?
At which land registry office must the petition be published: the one where the property lies?
How is publication done: a certified copy of the petition lodged with the registry, with a fee, and a registry receipt/certificate?
Is a certificate from the land registry attached to the petition or filed with the case, to prove publication?
By when must the publication be done: before filing the petition, at filing, or within a period after filing?
What is the sanction of failing to publish: inadmissibility of the petition (عدم القبول)?
Is the inadmissibility raised by the court of its own motion, or only by the opposing party?
Can the defect be cured later by publishing during the proceedings, and until when?
Does the sanction apply at first instance only, or also on appeal and cassation?
Is the publication required when the property is not published but a survey (cadastre) exists?
Is the plaintiff required to attach the title or deed of ownership and the cadastral extract?
Which section of the court hears real-property matters (land section) and what is its territorial court (court of the place of the property)?
Does the publication duty depend on whether a public body (State, wilaya, commune) is a party?
Does the claim fall under another procedure, such as an administrative court dispute over State property?
Are fees for publication a condition of registration of the petition?
Does the duty cover only the opening petition, or also appeals, cross-claims and interventions concerning the property?
Is a judgment on a published real right itself to be published at the registry afterwards?
Does the rule apply to a lease of real property, an eviction claim or a claim for possession protection?
What documents must the lawyer attach to the petition regarding the property (title, registry statement, plan)?
What happens if the defendant lives abroad or the owner is unknown?
Is there a time limit or limitation period attached to the claim over the real property that interacts with publication?
Which exits from the ordinary courts apply (administrative court, specialised commercial court) when real property is involved?
